title: Claude Opus 5.5 Tops Google Cloud's New Professional Engineering Benchmark
summary:
Google Cloud AI Research released a benchmark for AI agents called Physical-Engineering's Last Exam (PLE), comprising 85 tasks in mechanical, civil, electrical, and structural engineering. The test requires agents to generate professional deliverables, such as design packages that meet building-code and physics requirements, rather than answering textbook questions. Claude Opus 5.5 led the frontier models with a score of 48.3%, followed by GPT 6 Astra at 45.8%, Gemini 4 Argon at 40.6%, and Grok 4.7 at 30.1%.

The top performing agent configuration achieved an average score of 50.6% while utilizing 27M tokens and 63 minutes per task. The research team noted that PLE tasks are either written by practicing engineers or generated by an adversarial Creator-Solver agent pipeline and then validated by experts to increase difficulty.

selectedTweets.text:
Banger paper from Google Cloud AI Research on agents doing professional engineering work.

(bookmark it)

For professional engineering deliverables, the best agent configuration averages 50.6%, using 27M tokens and 63 minutes per task.

They introduce a benchmark called PLE (Physical-Engineering's Last Exam). It has 85 tasks across electrical, civil, structural, and mechanical engineering. Solving a task means producing a billable deliverable, such as a design package a licensed reviewer would sign off on, from a multi-format project corpus with physics and building-code requirements.

Some tasks are written end to end by practicing engineers. Others start from an engineer's problem statement, and an adversarial Creator-Solver agent pipeline builds the project environment, grader, and reference deliverables before experts validate them and make them harder.

Frontier models were tested under seven public agent harnesses. Most existing engineering benchmarks are textbook QA or toy design problems that leading agents already saturate.
